## Validation and Robustness

Use repeated grouped cross-validation and a final untouched test set. Compare errors by hull type, region, price quantile, and age band. Bootstrap confidence intervals for key effects. Repeat analyses with alternative age forms, price winsorization rules, exclusion of extremely sparse makes/variants, and region reweighting. Check whether conclusions persist under random rather than grouped splits; a large gap would indicate dependence leakage.

## Falsification Tests

- Permute prices relative to predictors; predictive performance should fall to baseline.
- Replace manufacture year with a randomized placebo; age effects should disappear.
- Compare residual distributions across hull types and regions.
- Test whether a model using only make/variant outperforms physically meaningful variables; if so, investigate memorization and sparse-category leakage.

## Reviewer Risks

Primary risks are target leakage through high-cardinality variant labels, overfitting from sparse makes, nonrepresentative advertising selection, confounding of hull type with length and geography, extrapolation beyond observed ages/lengths, and metric mismatch between log-scale training and USD-scale claims. Exact competition requirements remain a material documentation risk because the supplied excerpt is incomplete.
